actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: ControlWorld step units to advance; the upstream example sets world_control.step for one and world_control.multi_step otherwise
inputs.name: ticks

actions.name: step

actions.description: Request a pause of the simulated Gazebo world with the pinned step_simulation zero-step path; the method reports no result, so the receipt does not show that the world paused
actions.name: pause

outputs.description: True after step_simulation(0) returned; it returns None whether or not the ControlWorld call was answered
outputs.name: pause_requested

facts.text: The parent repository declares evs_gz_utils as a git submodule at path evs_gz_utils.
GzStepExample imports the ControlWorld service type from ros_gz_interfaces.srv.
GzStepExample declares a world_name ROS parameter and reads its string value from the parameter server.
GzStepExample builds the service name as /world/<world_name>/control and creates a ControlWorld client for it.
The stepping launch file bridges the parameterized world control service with type ros_gz_interfaces/srv/ControlWorld.
step_simulation sets world_control.pause to True on every request; it sets world_control.step to True for one step and world_control.multi_step to the requested count otherwise.
The constructor calls step_simulation with steps set to zero under the comment 'Ensure the simulation is paused'.

The service call spins without a timeout until the future completes and logs success when a result exists; it logs an error when the result is None, does not inspect any response field and returns None in both cases.
The model_state node creates an Odometry publisher on /evs/<model_name>/state and subscribes through a Gazebo node to /world/<world_name>/pose/info.
The model_state node writes the Gazebo position and orientation into the Odometry pose and derives linear and angular velocity from consecutive samples.
The model_state launch file bridges /clock as rosgraph_msgs/msg/Clock and sets use_sim_time.
The README identifies CrazySim 1.2x at commit 8ad9bb8 as the external simulation component.
The README states that no ROS is needed to control the CrazyFlie inside CrazySim.

determinism.notes: the fake records the requested step count deterministically, but the deployed Gazebo world, its physics and its RNG are external and the clone states no seed or state-hash contract; no replay claim is made

gaps: the fake is an analytic stand-in, not a recording: it does not replay captured ROS traffic and it opens no ROS graph, Gazebo world, ros_gz bridge or rclpy node
the upstream simulator is CrazySim/Gazebo, external to this clone (README.md:7); the clone contains only the ROS utility nodes, and no upstream simulator run was made
the clone states no Gazebo world max_step_size, so one ControlWorld step unit is not converted to simulated milliseconds; timestep_ms is 0 and ticks are service step units

the pinned example does not inspect the ControlWorld response and returns None for an answered and an unanswered call alike; a completed step is not proof that the world advanced, and the fake only sets local request flags

the pause request is not acknowledged, so the e-stop reports SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held; a pause that reaches Gazebo stops the world from stepping but not external ROS controllers, queued callbacks or CrazyFlie cflib clients, and it is not a sensed quiescence read-back

constructing GzStepExample needs a prior global rclpy.init(), waits without a timeout until /world/<world_name>/control appears (gz_step_example.py:28-29) and logs through the ROS logger; every step_simulation call spins without a timeout
the model_state Odometry observation on /evs/<model_name>/state is not served by this package; only the ControlWorld step and pause calls are bound
the cflib UDP control path in connection_example.py is not served; the README says no ROS is needed to control the CrazyFlie inside CrazySim (README.md:76)
only the fake backend is declared: the live path needs rclpy, ros_gz_interfaces and a running Gazebo world with the bridged service, none of which is installed or attached here

measures.description: ControlWorld step units requested since this backend was created
measures.name: tick

safe_state.description: No acknowledged safe state: the e-stop sends the constructor's ControlWorld pause request through step_simulation, which returns None whether or not the call was answered and never reads response.success, then reports SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held; a pause that reaches Gazebo leaves the world paused until something resumes it, unconfirmed, and external ROS controllers and cflib clients are not stopped.
